source: «Lettere di Carlo De Franceschi a Giovanni Kobler», printed 1928, pp. 107–207 — a hundred pages of letters written between 6 February 1873 and 19 June 1889, most from Parenzo. The family holds a scan. It was read through in September 2026 and the passages below are all of it that touches the family, its parish and its name.

quotes.it: Quel Giovanni Batt. De Franceschi venuto dalla Contea di Pisino, come Ella dice, intorno al 1740 è senz'altro proveniente dalla mia famiglia.
quotes.en: That Giovanni Battista De Franceschi who came from the County of Pazin, as you say, around 1740, is without doubt from my family.
quotes.why: The single sentence this archive has been working toward. The man the received account treats as a separate line is claimed, by the family's own historian, as one of them.

quotes.it: Suo padre, mio trisavolo, pure Giambattista del fu Leonardo, ebbe due figli Giampietro e Giambattista.
quotes.en: His father, my great-great-grandfather, also a Giambattista, son of the late Leonardo, had two sons: Giampietro and Giambattista.
quotes.why: Three generations named. And «Giambattista del fu Leonardo» is exactly the phrase the Gologorica register uses in 1769 — «Joannes Baptista Defranceschi filius Leonardi» — the entry that gives the casa-31 branch its byname «detti Leonardi».

quotes.it: Anche i miei derivano dalla Carnia, ma si stabilirono in Istria intorno al 1700.
quotes.en: Mine too derive from Carnia, but they settled in Istria around 1700.
quotes.why: The Gologorica family says of itself that it came from Carnia. The 1679 headmen's list already put a De Franceschi of Mione in the County of Pazin; this is the other end of the same road, stated by a descendant.

quotes.it: Il mio trisavolo fabbricò la nostra casa nel 1711 come da relativa iscrizione.
quotes.en: My great-great-grandfather built our house in 1711, as the inscription on it says.
quotes.why: The house on the Gologorica square, dated 1711 — built by Giambattista del fu Leonardo. The inscription this archive hoped somebody would photograph was read by Carlo himself.

quotes.it: Ma ve n'ha tuttodì a Mione e Muina della Carnia.
quotes.en: But there are still some of them today at Mione and Muina in Carnia.
quotes.why: Mione, named by Carlo De Franceschi. Muina is the next village along the same valley — both frazioni of Ovaro.

quotes.it: I nostri in origine erano da Bergamo, poi venuti in Carnia, dove avevano castelli, poi fortemente decaduti si dispersero.
quotes.en: Ours were originally from Bergamo, then came into Carnia, where they had castles, then fell badly and scattered.
quotes.why: The family's own tradition of itself, as told to Carlo by a cousin, Corrado, from papers kept in that branch. Bergamo before Carnia — a claim this archive had no way to reach.

quotes.it: Noi abbiamo stemma: nella parte superiore dello scudo una croce greca attraversata da due freccie, nell'inferiore un melagrano; sovra lo scudo elmo piumato.
quotes.en: We have arms: in the upper part of the shield a Greek cross crossed by two arrows, in the lower a pomegranate; above the shield a plumed helm.
quotes.why: The arms of this family, blazoned by its own head. Every heraldry catalogue consulted for this archive offered something else entirely.

quotes.it: Il nostro nome originario è veramente De Franceschi… Ma venuti negli stati austriaci sembrò alle autorità che volessero arrogarsi il titolo di nobiltà, non sapendo questi che il «de» in Italia aggiunto al nome esprime il casato, e non titolo nobiliare, onde essi nei decreti scrivevano Defranceschi.
quotes.en: Our original name is truly De Franceschi… But once they had come into the Austrian states it seemed to the authorities that they meant to arrogate a title of nobility — those authorities not knowing that in Italy the «de» added to a name expresses the house, not a title — so in their decrees they wrote Defranceschi.
quotes.why: The fused spelling explained by a man it was done to. Some signed Defranceschi for fear of the fine for claiming nobility they could not prove; others kept De Franceschi; a few went to plain Franceschi.

pedigree: the eponym; his son is «Giambattista del fu Leonardo»
Carlo's great-great-grandfather. Built the Gologorica house in 1711. Two sons.
the elder; a fedecommesso was settled on him in the custom of the time

the younger; meant for the priesthood, studied at Fiume, «felt a vocation for the sword instead» and volunteered in Maria Theresa's army. Made castellan of Bribir for his service; married a lady of the D'Agnese family.
descendants: Chancellor of the County of Pazin in the last century
known to Carlo in 1848; employed at the Trieste customs house
moved to Zadar and went into the revenue service; the Zadar De Franceschi keep the names Giambattista and Vincenzo
port captain of Fiume — descended, Carlo thought, not from Giambattista but from Valentino, who came to Fiume directly from Carnia, and who told Carlo his ancestors came from there
a De Franceschi drawing master and perhaps engineer at the Fiume gymnasium when Carlo studied there, 1820–1826

correction.heading: And then, two months later, Carlo corrected himself
correction.lead: The pedigree above comes from the letter of 10 November 1876. On 31 January 1877 Carlo wrote again, having had more from Kobler, and withdrew part of it — which this archive had been repeating as his conclusion.
correction.quote: Adesso, la di Lei mercè, sono in chiaro riguardo al ramo della mia famiglia stabilitasi a Fiume. Io confondeva il primo Giambattista col secondo di lui figlio, di nome pure Giovanni, ritenendo che già quello era a Bribir. E mi rincresce assai di non aver saputo che il vivente Francesco sia mio terzo cugino.
correction.en: Now, thanks to you, I am clear about the branch of my family settled at Fiume. I was confusing the first Giambattista with his son, also called Giovanni, believing that the first was already at Bribir. And I am very sorry not to have known that the living Francesco is my third cousin.
correction.why: So Francesco, harbour-master of Fiume, is not descended from a Valentino who came from Carnia in 1739. He is Carlo's own third cousin, four generations down from the same Giambattista del fu Leonardo. Carlo had spent five years living in Fiume knowing the man only slightly, and says so with real regret: «avrei fatto con esso Francesco relazione ben più stretta» — I would have made a far closer connection with him.

trees.note: Carlo drew the two lines side by side in the letter. They are printed as two columns and this is how they read.

gologorica.heading: What his family actually did at Gologorica
gologorica.lead: The single most useful thing in the correspondence, and it is buried in a technical exchange about the Urbaria of the County of Pisino, dated 19 March 1877.
gologorica.quote: Negli Urbari non compariscono Gollogorizza, Tupliaco e Scopliaco, perchè ne era Dominus il vescovo di Pedena. A questi Gollogorizza pagava non già la decima, ma un invariabile annuo corrispettivo in vino, frumento, avena, agnelli, galline ed uova, locchè chiamavasi «affitto fermo», forse per seguito antico accordo. Questo affitto fermo sino alla soppressione del vescovato veniva percepito dalla mia famiglia a titolo di affittanza, rinnovata da ogni vescovo, a cui pagava il convenuto importo. Prima che Gollogorizza fosse dei vescovi di Pedena, era un bene della nobile famiglia Schnal di Pisino.
gologorica.en: Gologorica, Tupljak and Škopljak do not appear in the Urbaria, because the bishop of Pedena was their Lord. To him Gologorica paid not a tithe but a fixed annual render in wine, wheat, oats, lambs, hens and eggs, which was called the «affitto fermo» — the firm rent — perhaps following some ancient agreement. Until the suppression of the bishopric this firm rent was collected by my family as lessees, the lease renewed by every bishop, to whom we paid the agreed sum. Before Gologorica belonged to the bishops of Pedena it was a holding of the noble Schnal family of Pisino.
gologorica.why: This is what the De Franceschi were at Gologorica. Not landowners and not peasants — the men who farmed the bishop's rent, holding a lease renewed at every episcopal succession, collecting wine, grain, oats, lambs, hens and eggs from their neighbours and paying the bishop a fixed sum. It is a middleman's position, and a durable one: it ran until the diocese of Pedena was suppressed in 1788. It also explains why the bishops styled themselves «Dominus Gollaegoritiae» and why a village of a few dozen houses turns up in a bishop's title at all — a point Carlo also makes, from the other end, in his book.

bells.heading: He began his collection of Istrian bell inscriptions with his own village
bells.lead: From the letter of 10 November 1876, written at Gologorica — «mio luogo natale», my birthplace — where he had gone to spend a whole month with his family after a bereavement.

rows.text: «Una porta in caratteri gotici rotondi l'epigrafe 1364: Magister Nicholaus me fecit.» One carries, in round gothic letters, the date 1364 and the words Master Nicholaus made me. «Ella vede che è ben vecchia» — you see it is very old indeed. A second bell by the same Nicolò and his brother Giovanni, a few years later, hangs at Zarečje.

Three inscriptions on one bell. In square gothic: «A fulgure et tempestate libera nos Domine» — from lightning and tempest deliver us, O Lord. In round gothic: «Facta sub Plebano Georgio Challigarich opus Ioannis Albinus 1573» — made under the parish priest Juraj Kaligarić, the work of Ivan Albinus. And beneath those, four Glagolitic letters, which Carlo sent to Volčić to interpret and never reports an answer for.

bells.close: Carlo's plan was to collect the bell inscriptions of the whole of Istria. He started with the bells he had grown up under.

bribir.heading: The siege of Bribir
bribir.lead: Giambattista, the brother meant for the priesthood, was made castellan of Bribir after the Seven Years' War. Carlo tells what happened there as a story he had from his elders.
bribir.text: «È interessante il racconto della sua difesa con pochi servi contro una feroce banda di masnadieri forte di 40 e più uomini, che assaltarono e presero finalmente il castello, dopo che egli dall'ultimo suo servo rimasto vivo fu calato nel fondo d'una torre, dove i ladroni nol poterono trovare.» — The account of his defence, with a few servants, against a fierce band of brigands forty and more strong, who attacked and at last took the castle, after his last surviving servant had lowered him into the bottom of a tower where the robbers could not find him.
bribir.coda: And then the other half of it, which is why the story survived: «Il vecchio mio professore Potosniak mi narrava d'aver dato gli estremi sacramenti al terribile condottiero di quella banda, morto assai vecchio, e che gli espose la lunghissima serie di tutti i suoi misfatti.» — My old teacher Potočnjak told me he had given the last rites to the terrible leader of that band, dead very old, who laid out for him the very long series of all his crimes. A branch of the family lived at Bribir until about 1836, then moved to Zadar.

razvod.heading: A scholar's opinion worth recording
razvod.text: Twice in these letters Carlo states, flatly, that the Istrian Razvod — the famous boundary act dated 1325, one of the oldest documents in the Croatian language and a monument of Glagolitic writing — is not genuine: «Gli studii che ho fatto sul famoso Razvod istriano del 1325 mi inducono a ritenerlo un'impostura elaborata intorno al 1500 nel castello di Pisino.» An imposture put together around 1500 in Pisino castle. Kobler held it authentic, and Carlo notes the disagreement politely — «che io per motivi a Lei noti ammetto come genuino» he writes of Kobler's position, not his own.
razvod.why: It has no bearing on the family. It is here because it shows what kind of reader Carlo was, and because it is the strongest opinion he expresses anywhere in a hundred pages of otherwise mild correspondence.

otherhalf.heading: And now the other half of it
otherhalf.lead: Everything above is Carlo writing to Kobler, from the 1928 printing. Kobler's own letters — the questions Carlo was answering — were edited by Jakov Jelinčić and published in three parts in the Vjesnik of the Rijeka and Pazin archives in 1977, 1978 and after. They are open access, and this archive did not know they existed until September 2026.
otherhalf.never: Jelinčić opens with a fact worth sitting with. Kobler corresponded with De Franceschi for sixteen years — and «čini se da se Kobler i de Franceschi usprkos obostranoj želji nikada nisu osobno upoznali»: it seems that Kobler and de Franceschi, despite wanting to on both sides, never met in person.

question.heading: The question that produced the famous answer
question.text: Kobler had gone through the civic records of Fiume and listed every Defranceschi household he could find there. Then he sent the list to Carlo and asked, in four words: «È forse Lei un Discendente?» — Are you perhaps a descendant? Carlo's reply is the letter this archive has built half its Carnia argument on.

valentino.heading: And Kobler's second entry is a document, not a tradition
valentino.text: «Valentino Defranceschi, venuto dalla Carnia, fu fatto Cittadino nel 1739, e colla moglie Elena ebbe 10 figli e 4 figlie, aveva casa in contrada dei Capuccini e vigna in Plase, fabbricò nel 1764 la Capella di S. Elena, fece per se tomba nel Duomo con epigrafe nel 1785 e morì nel 1785.»
valentino.en: Valentino Defranceschi, come from Carnia, was made a Citizen in 1739; by his wife Elena he had ten sons and four daughters; he had a house in the Capuchins' quarter and a vineyard at Plase; in 1764 he built the Chapel of St Helen; in 1785 he made himself a tomb in the Duomo with an epigraph; and he died in 1785. His son Ignazio married Giuseppa Danezello, was a Civic Representative in 1783, and died in 1785 aged forty.
valentino.why: This matters more than anything Carlo says about his own ancestors. The Carnia page of this archive has been resting on a single document — the headmen's list of 1679. Here is a second, from a different researcher working a different record set: Kobler, reading the civic registers of Fiume, states as a matter of record that a Defranceschi came from Carnia and was made a citizen in 1739. It does not connect anybody to this family. It does mean that Carnians of this surname demonstrably moved into the Kvarner in the eighteenth century, which is the whole mechanism the family's own tradition describes.
valentino.then: And Valentino left two things that can still be looked for: the Chapel of St Helen at Rijeka, built 1764, and his tomb in the cathedral with an epigraph of 1785.

otherhalf.source: Jakov Jelinčić, «Korespondencija Giovanni Kobler — Carlo De Franceschi», Vjesnik historijskih arhiva u Rijeci i Pazinu XXI (1977) pp. 181–196, XXII (1978) pp. 37–57, and part III. Open access on Hrčak.
